draft.title: z-scores
card: A z-score tells how many standard deviations a value is from the mean. z = (x − μ) ÷ σ, where x is the value, μ is the mean and σ is the standard deviation.
A positive z-score means the value is above the mean. A negative z-score means it is below the mean. A z-score of 0 means it equals the mean.
Example: a test has mean 60 and standard deviation 8. A mark of 76 has z = (76 − 60) ÷ 8 = 16 ÷ 8 = 2, so it is 2 standard deviations above the mean.
A z-score has no units, so it lets you compare values from different distributions. The higher z-score is further above its own mean, relative to its spread.
draft.remember: z is the distance from the mean, measured in standard deviations.

a.q: A variable has mean 50 and standard deviation 5. What is the z-score of the value 42?
a.why: z = (42 − 50) ÷ 5 = −8 ÷ 5 = −1.6. The value is below the mean, so z is negative. Giving 1.6 drops the sign, and −8 forgets to divide by the standard deviation.
a.clue: Subtract the mean first, then divide by the standard deviation.

b.q: Priya scores 68 in Maths, where the mean is 56 and σ = 6. She scores 75 in Science, where the mean is 65 and σ = 8. In which subject did she do better compared with her class?
opts: Maths, because its z-score of 2 is higher than 1.25
Science, because 75 is a higher mark than 68
Science, because its mean of 65 is higher
Neither, because the two tests have different means
b.why: Maths: z = (68 − 56) ÷ 6 = 2. Science: z = (75 − 65) ÷ 8 = 1.25. The higher z-score is further above its own mean, so Maths is better. Comparing raw marks is tempting, but the two tests have different means and spreads.
b.clue: Work out both z-scores before comparing.

b.best: Maths, because its z-score of 2 is higher than 1.25
